question: What will the first reported earnings per share after September 2026 be for the following companies? (Meta)

calls.reasoning: Meta disclosed (Aug 26, 2026 settlement with state AGs) that it expects to accrue ~$10B legal expense in Q3 2026, not in its prior outlook. Ex-charge Q3 GAAP EPS ~6.7-7.1 (revenue guide $61-64B, consensus ~$63.3B; FY expense guide $165-169B implies ~$44B Q3 opex; tax 15-17%; ~2.57B diluted shares). The $10B charge is ~$3.9/share pre-tax, so GAAP diluted EPS likely ~2.8-3.6, far below the 5.345 lower bound. Consensus $6.67-6.77 headlines are adjusted (ex-legal). I believe >=90% of mass is below range but the format caps p_below_lower at 0.5; in-range percentiles are clustered near the lower bound. No Polymarket/Manifold market; Kalshi page shows $6.39 consensus (terms unverified, likely adjusted).
calls.dossier:
- Resolves off GAAP diluted EPS in Meta's Q3 2026 earnings release (expected Oct 28, 2026 after close; some sources say Oct 21), not adjusted/consensus EPS.
- Event window: quarter Jul 1 -> Sep 30, 2026 (complete as of 2026-10-17); release date ~Oct 28.
- Aug 26, 2026 (CNBC/Yahoo/Variety): Meta settled state AG youth social-media addiction litigation, up to $18B over 10 years (~$12.7B fixed, $5.3B contingent on YouTube/TikTok changes). Meta stated it expects to 'accrue a legal expense of approximately $10 billion in the third quarter of 2026 related to the agreement,' not previously taken into account in outlook.
- Q2 2026 release (SEC 8-K, Jul 2026): revenue $60.80B, expenses $42.03B (incl. $2.40B legal charges, $1.18B severance), op income $18.78B, tax rate 16%, net income $15.85B, diluted EPS $6.18, diluted shares 2,566M. Q3 revenue guide $61-64B; FY26 total expenses $165-169B; tax 15-17% for remaining quarters; capex $130-145B.
- Q1 2026: expenses $33.44B, op income $22.87B, diluted EPS $10.44 including $8.03B tax benefit (ex-benefit $7.31).
- H1 2026 expenses $75.47B -> H2 implied $89.5-93.5B under guide (ex-$10B accrual).
- Consensus EPS headlines Oct 2026: $6.67 (Mint/Zacks-style), $6.77 (Bloomberg via elEconomista), $6.74-6.77 described as adjusted excluding legal charges (Admiral Markets), $5.94 among 44 analysts (Alphastreet, falling from $7.06 90 days earlier), Kalshi-listed $6.39. Revenue consensus ~$63.2-63.3B.
- Admiral Markets: $10B pre-tax charge ~ $3.90/share GAAP.
- Tax deductibility of the settlement unknown (government settlements often partially nondeductible under IRC 162(f) except restitution).
- Precedent: Q3 2025 GAAP EPS $1.05 after $15.93B one-time tax charge (vs ~$7.25 ex-charge).
- Searched but not found: Meta's own updated Q3 expense outlook including the accrual; exact tax treatment; Kalshi contract terms (page errored).

calls.reasoning: Underlying Q3 2026 EPS consensus is ~$6.6-6.8, and BofA's estimate before the charge was $7.08; Meta usually beats. But Meta disclosed it will accrue a ~$10B legal expense in Q3 for the Aug 26, 2026 settlement with 52 state AGs, which it did not include in its Q2 guidance. With 2.566B diluted shares that is $2.96 (deductible) to $3.90 (non-deductible) per share, so GAAP EPS is likely ~$2.9-4.3 (BofA GAAP estimate $3.79). This is far below the 5.345 lower bound; my true P(below) is ~0.96, capped at 0.5 by the payload format. Percentiles are conditional on landing in range, a scenario that needs the charge mostly left out of Q3, so they sit near the lower bound. No human market found on Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or bookmakers.

calls.reconciliation: Main dispute: whether the ~$10B Q3 legal accrual lands in Q3 GAAP EPS. Run 3 left it out; runs 1-2 included it. Search 1 (Bitget/CNBC/Variety) confirmed Meta's statement that it will accrue ~$10B in Q3 2026. Search 2 (Admiral Markets/Alphastreet/TradingView) confirmed JPMorgan models the $10B provision outside the $165-169B guidance, and that the $6.28-6.76 consensus figures don't consistently include it. The dispute settles in favour of runs 1-2. Tax deductibility was not found and stays a judgment call that doesn't matter here: both cases land far below the range. The report date (Oct 21 vs Oct 28) is unresolved but irrelevant, since both are after Sep 30.
